title: $500/Month Side Income: What It's Worth in 10 Years
description:
What is $500 a month of side income worth in 10 years? Spend it and that's $60,000 of extras. Invest it at an assumed 7% a year and it could grow to about $85,526: your own $60,000 plus about $25,526 of growth. Most of that growth comes late: about $190 in year one versus $5,380 in year ten.

Assumptions (our own math): $500 left after tax, invested at the end of every month for 10 years; a steady 7% yearly return (at 4% it would be about $73,348, at 10% about $99,932); no fees, no tax on the growth, no inflation adjustment. Real returns vary, can be negative and are not guaranteed. Taxes: in the US, side income is usually subject to income tax, and if you're self-employed with net earnings of $400 or more, self-employment tax of 15.3% (12.4% Social Security + 2.9% Medicare; IRS Tax Topic 554). Set tax money aside before you invest; rules differ in other countries. Educational only, not financial advice.

scenes.say: Five hundred a month on the side: spent, or eighty-five thousand dollars?
Say a side gig nets five hundred a month, after tax.
Spend it all: sixty thousand dollars over ten years.
Invest it instead, at an assumed seven percent a year...
...and it could grow to about eighty-five thousand dollars.
Here's the catch: early years feel like nothing.
Year one, growth adds under two hundred dollars. Year ten, over five thousand.
Sixty thousand is your own money. Time adds about twenty-five thousand more.
No shortcut. Just a steady habit and patience.
So what will your five hundred become?
